A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the revised title. All 19 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP and MoCo-v2 retrieval experiments, ten-dataset classification results, HCL comparisons, and cross-image sampling ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds LVIS retrieval results and evaluation of fine-tuned HCL.

M1.justification: The pairwise hierarchy construction, shared encoder, hyperbolic projection, and bidirectional contrastive angle loss are retained. Explicit exponential-map boxes in Figure 3 and the newly specified learnable temperature clarify implementation without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds out-of-domain same-class and hierarchical retrieval on LVIS, covering 1,203 categories and reporting 897 categories absent from OpenImages. HierOpenImages and the ten single-class datasets remain; the latter evaluation is renamed, not replaced.

E2.justification: v2 adds HCL fine-tuned on HierOpenImages to both retrieval comparisons. Unmodified HCL with cosine similarity and hyperbolic distance was already evaluated in v1 Appendix B.4 and Tables 4–5; its appearance in v2 main Tables 1–2 is largely relocation.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 revises the reported HierOpenImages candidate counts from approximately 0.33M full images and 0.6M crops to 59,691 and 330,063. Fixed-k hierarchical evaluation drops precision while retaining recall and OT distance. LVIS introduces its own candidate set and hierarchy thresholds. These are reported protocol changes; rerunning the retained experiments is not established.

E4.justification: The cross-image sampling ablation and Figure 5 curves are retained, but the appendix ablation loses fixed-k precision results. Qualitative retrieval analysis expands from four queries in v1 Figure 8 to ten in v2 Figure 9, retaining the original examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Random sampling descriptions and statistical uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds LVIS and fine-tuned HCL results, removes fixed-k precision entries, and revises several baseline scores. For example, CLIP's top-150k recall/OT changes from 51.42/24.30 to 51.33/23.81. The proposed models' retained quantitative results and ten-dataset scores match. Revised candidate counts prevent treating baseline differences as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the Lorentz model's ambient-space description from Euclidean space to pseudo-Euclidean Minkowski space and updates Equation 1 accordingly. It removes the geodesics characterization. The entailment relations, loss equations, and Wasserstein formulation remain substantively unchanged; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The principal hierarchy-learning and evaluation-metric contributions remain. v2 adds an explicit novelty claim of being the first model to generalize to out-of-domain image hierarchies and reframes the generalization contribution around unseen data rather than zero-shot classification.

C2.justification: v1 dismisses HCL as unsuitable for comparison; v2 interprets its poor performance after fine-tuning as difficulty learning complex hierarchies. v2 also explains incompatibilities with text-encoder and predefined single-class hierarchy methods. It removes v1's stronger interpretation of classification results as demonstrating stable, reliable predictions and a well-conditioned latent space.

D1.justification: v2 specifies learnable temperature initialization at 0.07, explains selection of the existing 80% overlap threshold, and documents LVIS construction and a Gradio interface. It removes the explicit most-granular-parent rule for resolving multiple parents. Projection size and learnable curvature disclosures are retained in the appendix.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for LVIS, Gradio, and Ge et al.'s robust contrastive learning work. Related work more explicitly distinguishes multi-object hierarchy learning from predefined single-class hierarchies and identifies HCL as the closest approach. The earlier literature coverage is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title, clarifies model names, replaces misleading zero-shot classification terminology with image-only retrieval terminology, and reorganizes HCL and generalization discussion. Several explanations are shortened or rewritten, but the overall section sequence and most methodological exposition remain.

P2.justification: v2 consolidates HCL comparisons into the main tables, substantially restructures hierarchical-result tables, and adds the LVIS table. Figure 3 explicitly depicts exponential mapping; a Gradio screenshot and category catalogue are added, and the appendix retrieval montage expands. Several existing figures are relocated or relabeled rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: LVIS provides direct evidence of transfer to unseen hierarchies, and fine-tuning HCL on HierOpenImages strengthens the comparison. Clearer image-only retrieval terminology also improves interpretation of retained results. These gains are tempered by removed precision entries and unexplained revisions to candidate counts and baseline scores, yielding a limited net improvement.
